newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of Japan's March tankan survey.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of Japan's March tankan survey.

text.p: The following is a selection of economists' and analysts' initial reactions to the Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s "tankan" short-term corporate survey in March, released on Wednesday, which showed that the business outlook among major manufacturers had improved since the previous survey in November.
JANE BERRYMAN, SENIOR ANALYST FIXED INCOME, TECHNICAL DATA

"We were expecting a moderately positive reading (for major manufacturers). The surprise came in the non-manufacturing side. Most people were expecting about a flat reading and we ended up with a minus six."
The March diffusion index for major manufacturers was plus two, while the index for major non-manufacturers was minus six.

Berryman said: "JGBs are surrendering some ground now, having already priced most of the results of the report, but I think we're going to end up seeing (JGB) prices recover because of the non- manufacturing side still continuing to look quite weak."
RICHARD JERRAM, CHIEF ECONOMIST, ING BARINGS

"As expected, the figures deteriorated. It seems that people are worried about the tax rises from April. On the back of this type of number it's hard to see that the Bank of Japan will move anytime soon (to tighten credit)."

Jerram added: "The message from the tankan is that (because of) the yen's fall of 10 percent in the four months since the previous survey, the external sector is doing very well, but everything else is doing pretty badly still."
TETSURO SAWANO, ECONOMIST, NIKKO RESEARCH CENTRE

"The fall in non-manufacturing can probably be attributed to the fact that there wasn't much of a consumer rush ahead of the sales tax at the time of survey -- even though there was a bit of a rush afterwards. The retail and distribution sectors were probably affected by this"

"The June figures were pretty much as forecast -- with the uncertainty created by the sales tax the indices were bound to get worse. The major manufacturing index (forecast) for June was surprising in that it only fell as far as it did."
